source_resources.title: Hugging Face LLM Evaluation Guidebook (legacy edition)
source_resources.author: Hugging Face evaluation-guidebook contributors
source_resources.relevant_timestamp: contents/automated-benchmarks/designing-your-automatic-evaluation.md: Choosing a dataset; Choosing an inference method; Choosing a prompt
source_resources.version_or_verification_date: Public edition checked 2026-11-01; moving pages may change
source_resources.permission_basis: External hyperlink only; no third-party prose, exercises, code or translations are imported.
source_resources.prerequisites: Held-out data, basic language-model metrics and experimental comparisons.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Teaching-oriented evaluation design and reproducibility guidance complements the benchmark papers. Stable methodological chapters only; not a current tooling/version reference.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: README says no longer maintained. The replacement OpenEvals Space was not verified as containing the guidebook; its license and content are not substituted. No bootstrap derivation is claimed.
source_resources.safe_fallback: Use the original localized explanations, exercises and checks already present in this activity; no external account or purchase is required for that fallback.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: HELM
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Retained for the multi-metric framework; the guidebook makes practical choices easier to teach.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: LM Evaluation Harness
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Useful implementation cross-check; tool configuration alone does not teach metric choice or evaluator limitations.

source_resources.title: Holistic Evaluation of Language Models (HELM)
source_resources.author: Percy Liang, Rishi Bommasani, Tony Lee, Dimitris Tsipras, Dilara Soylu, et al.
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful academic citation of open access benchmark taxonomy.
source_resources.prerequisites: Language model architectures, multi-metric benchmarking, prompt formatting.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Original holistic benchmark framework establishing multi-metric evaluation across accuracy, calibration, robustness, fairness, toxicity, and efficiency under standardized prompt interfaces.
source_resources.safe_fallback: Complete evaluation taxonomies, multi-metric scorecards, and standardized baseline protocol definitions are implemented directly in curriculum lessons.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Wang et al. GLUE: A Multi-Task Benchmark and Analysis Platform for Natural Language Understanding
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: NLU benchmark focused on classification and regression fine-tuning; HELM addresses generative autoregressive foundation models.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Wang et al. SuperGLUE: A Stickier Benchmark for General-Purpose Language Understanding Systems
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Harder successor to GLUE but still constrained to classification; HELM formalizes multi-dimensional open-ended generation evaluation.

source_resources.relevant_timestamp: Section 1.1 HELM and Section 2 Preliminaries (2.1 Scenarios, 2.3 Metrics)

source_resources.title: Measuring Massive Multitask Language Understanding (MMLU)
source_resources.author: Dan Hendrycks, Collin Burns, Steven Basart, Andy Zou, Mantas Mazeika, Dawn Song, Jacob Steinhardt
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful academic citation of open access benchmark specification.
source_resources.prerequisites: Multiple-choice evaluation, conditional log-likelihood, 5-shot prompt templates.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Standardized benchmark spanning 57 subjects across STEM, humanities, and social sciences; foundational reference for few-shot multiple-choice evaluation formulation.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Freely available on arXiv and GitHub.
source_resources.safe_fallback: MMLU prompt formatting, 5-shot exemplar layout, log-likelihood ranking algorithms, and category aggregation logic are fully explained in lesson materials.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Zhong et al. AGIEval: A Human-Centric Benchmark for Evaluating Foundation Models Towards General Intelligence
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Evaluates qualification exam questions; MMLU provides a widely used multi-task knowledge baseline.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Srivastava et al. Beyond the Imitation Game: Quantifying and Extrapolating the Capabilities of Language Models (BIG-bench)
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Enormous community benchmark with high task heterogeneity; MMLU offers a focused, standard 57-subject knowledge distribution.

source_resources.relevant_timestamp: Section 3 A Multitask Test and Section 4 Experiments

source_resources.title: Training Verifiers to Solve Math Word Problems (GSM8K)
source_resources.author: Karl Cobbe, Vineet Kosaraju, Mohammad Bavarian, Mark Chen, Heewoo Jun, et al.
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful academic citation and open source evaluation harness reference.
source_resources.prerequisites: Elementary grade school mathematics, multi-step word problem reasoning, answer extraction formatting.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Defines the GSM8K dataset and its final-answer format ('#### <answer>') that the lesson's answer parser and exact-match scorer rely on.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Freely available on arXiv and GitHub.
source_resources.safe_fallback: GSM8K multi-step problem templates, calculation traces, and exact regex extraction routines are fully coded in lesson text.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Patel et al. Are NLP Models really able to Solve Simple Math Word Problems? (SVAMP)
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Adversarial perturbations on math problems; GSM8K provides the standard training/testing distribution for multi-step reasoning.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Hendrycks et al. Measuring Mathematical Problem Solving With the MATH Dataset
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: High-school competition math requiring complex LaTeX typesetting; GSM8K isolates core elementary arithmetic reasoning chains.

source_resources.relevant_timestamp: Section 2 Dataset; Appendix F Verifier Visualization (solutions end with '#### <answer>')

activities.title: Review Drill: LoRA Math, Freezing, Optimizer Memory, and Merging (Days 64-66)

source_resources.title: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
source_resources.author: Edward J. Hu, Yelong Shen, Phillip Wallis, Zeyuan Allen-Zhu, Yuanzhi Li, Shean Wang, Lu Wang, Weizhu Chen
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful academic reference under arXiv open access terms.
source_resources.prerequisites: Matrix factorization, rank, linear layers, and transformer attention.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Primary literature introducing Low-Rank Adaptation, establishing parameter decomposition W = W0 + (alpha/r)*BA, initialization strategies, and zero inference latency merging.
source_resources.safe_fallback: Complete matrix derivations, tensor dimensions, and pure PyTorch LoRALinear modules are implemented directly in lesson code.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Houlsby et al. Parameter-Efficient Transfer Learning for NLP (Series Adapters)
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Introduces bottleneck adapter layers in series, which introduces unavoidable inference latency overhead; LoRA's parallel formulation merges with zero latency.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Li & Liang: Prefix-Tuning: Optimizing Continuous Prompts for Generation
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Prepends virtual prompt tokens; reduces available context length, unlike LoRA which preserves full sequence capacity.

source_resources.relevant_timestamp: Section 4.1 Low-Rank-Parametrized Update Matrices (W0 + BA, B initialized to zero, scaling by alpha/r); Section 4.2 Applying LoRA to Transformer (frozen W0, VRAM and checkpoint-size reduction)

source_resources.title: PEFT: State-of-the-art Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning Methods
source_resources.author: Sourab Mangrulkar, Sylvain Gugger, Lysandre Debut, Younes Belkada, Sayak Paul, Benjamin Bossan
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful external reference under Apache-2.0 open-source terms.
source_resources.prerequisites: PyTorch nn.Module, Hugging Face transformers, and LoRA equations.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Widely adopted open-source library implementing LoRA configuration classes (LoraConfig), get_peft_model, and adapter serialization.
source_resources.safe_fallback: Standalone, zero-dependency PyTorch implementations of LoRALinear layers and save/reload logic are provided in curriculum scripts.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Microsoft LoRA Original PyTorch Package (loralib)
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Original reference code by Hu et al.; PEFT expands this to broader multi-model ecosystem integration.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Lit-GPT LoRA implementation (Lightning AI)
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: High-performance clean implementation; compared alongside PEFT for modular code architecture.

source_resources.title: Stanford Alpaca: An Instruction-following LLaMA Model
source_resources.author: Rohan Taori, Ishaan Gulrajani, Tianyi Zhang, Yann Dubois, Xuechen Li, Carlos Guestrin, Percy Liang, Tatsunori B. Hashimoto
source_resources.license: Copyright Stanford CRFM (blog post; no open license stated)
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful external linking to a copyrighted blog post; no text is imported.
source_resources.prerequisites: Supervised fine-tuning, instruction formatting, and LoRA fundamentals.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Original open recipe demonstrating lightweight instruction fine-tuning of open models, establishing prompt/response templates, batch scheduling, and learning rate ranges.
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Publicly hosted on Stanford CRFM website.
source_resources.safe_fallback: Complete instruction templates, JSONL formatting scripts, and learning rate schedules are self-contained in curriculum materials.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Vicuna: An Open-Source Chatbot Impressing GPT-4 (LMSYS)
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Multi-turn ShareGPT tuning recipe; Alpaca provides simpler, single-turn clarity ideal for foundational instruction tuning study.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Databricks Dolly 15k Dataset & Training Recipe
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Commercially permissive crowdsourced dataset; Alpaca established the academic instruction tuning standard.
